title: Expand perf-canary coverage to top 10 production models (post-threshold tuning)
creator: Talia Benson
description:
After Phase 1 (single region + 2–3 models) has stabilized (threshold tuning + reduced false positives), expand the prod perf-canary model set to cover the top 10 production models.

This ticket is specifically about:
- Selecting and enabling the additional models in control-plane config per region/tier
- Ensuring baseline artifacts exist per model/runtime/SKU (and region if required)
- Validating overhead stays within the target budget (<0.5% GPU capacity per region for covered models)
- Verifying dashboards/alerts remain usable (no cardinality blowups, no alert storms)

Non-goals:
- Changing baseline strategy/ADR (handled in ENG-4874 / ADR)
- Adding new metric dimensions beyond what was approved in the cardinality audit

Primary stakeholders:
- Runtime perf canary TL: Noah Patel
- Scheduling signals: Sofia Ivanova
- Kernel attribution tags: Hiro Tanaka
- Baselines pipeline: Nadia Rahman
- Fleet/capacity: Vanessa Ortiz
- SRE readiness: Sean Gallagher / Rafael Mendes

Key references:
- Design doc: sources/confluence/eng-serving-runtime/kernel-and-scheduling/perf-regression-canary-design.json
- ADR (baselines/thresholds): sources/confluence/architecture-and-standards/decision-records/adr-perf-canary-baseline-and-thresholds.json
- Dashboard spec: sources/confluence/eng-platform/dashboards-and-alerts/perf-canary-dashboards-spec.json
- Validation plan: sources/confluence/eng-serving-runtime/benchmarking-and-perf-suite/perf-canary-validation-plan.json
- Cardinality audit: sources/google_drive/shared_drives/engineering/observability/perf-canary-metrics-cardinality-audit.json

Proposed rollout shape:
- Expand in the same region as Phase 1 first, then carry forward to additional regions after 48–72h of clean signals.
- Enable new models in 2 waves (top 5, then top 10) to reduce blast radius and isolate model-specific variance.

Proposed initial model candidates (final list to be confirmed with Quentin/model registry + usage analytics):
- Top chat models (hosted): 4–5
- 1–2 embedding/rerank models if they share runtime path and are high-volume
- 2–3 "high-risk" models with recent kernel/scheduler work (optional; only if overhead budget holds)

Open questions:
- Do we need region-specific thresholds for any of the top 10 due to SKU mix differences (e.g., H100 vs L40S pools)?
- For Dedicated pools, do we enable the canary with a separate tier label, or keep Hosted-only for this wave to avoid skew?
- Baseline refresh cadence: do we pin fixed baselines for 2 weeks after expansion, or allow rolling updates with guardrails?
acceptance_criteria:
1) Top 10 model list is finalized and merged into control-plane canary config for Phase 1 region with audit trail.
2) Baseline artifacts exist for each enabled model keyed by (model, model_version, runtime_build, hardware_sku) and are retrievable by perf-canary.
3) Canary overhead measured at the region level remains below 0.5% GPU capacity (24h window) with documented methodology (queries + assumptions).
4) No increase in telemetry cost/cardinality beyond approved label set; Grafana dashboards remain responsive.
5) Warning alerts (non-paging) fire correctly on synthetic injected regression test OR staging replay, and do not flap under steady state.
6) Rollout checklist updated with steps to enable top-10 wave and validated by SRE sign-off.
7) Post-expansion summary comment added to this ticket with: enabled models, baseline versions, overhead numbers, and any threshold exceptions.
implementation_notes:
Work breakdown (suggested):
- Model selection + gating
  - Pull top-10 models by last-14d request volume + revenue-weighted token volume; sanity check with Product.
  - Confirm canonical model+version IDs with model registry to avoid baseline churn (Quentin).
  - Confirm "high-risk" additions (recent kernel changes) are not overlapping with major runtime release windows.

- Config + validation
  - Update control-plane model allowlist for canary targets (per region) with a 2-wave rollout (top5 -> top10).
  - Validate config via dry-run/validation endpoint (avoid prior config validation errors).
  - Ensure safe-guard against accidental wide fanout (region/SKU scoped).

- Baselines
  - For each model, generate baseline distributions from prod-like load job and publish to baseline store.
  - Record baseline lineage: commit SHA / runtime build tag / kernel selection tag(s) / SKU.
  - Ensure minimum sample size is achieved and variance captured; if a model is too noisy, document and either widen thresholds or defer.

- Capacity/overhead
  - Validate QPS caps and concurrency settings for expanded set; ensure canary does not compete with customer traffic.
  - Measure GPU-time overhead (preferred), or infer from request rate x measured runtime_ms with confidence bounds.
  - If overhead > budget, adjust: reduce run frequency, reduce prompt set size, or drop low-signal models.

- Dashboards/alerts
  - Add/verify per-model panels for the expanded model set (keep dashboards usable; avoid 10x panel explosion if possible via templating).
  - Keep paging disabled for this expansion wave unless SRE explicitly approves; warnings only.
  - Verify alert payloads include correct links (dashboard, logs, trace) for each new model.

risks_and_mitigations:
Risk: overhead breaches (<0.5% GPU) once top-10 fanout is enabled.
Mitigation: enforce QPS caps per model; stagger scheduling; keep a global capacity budget; roll out in waves; keep a kill-switch documented and tested.

Risk: alert noise due to model-specific variance (prompt-shape sensitivity, caching differences, different decode lengths).
Mitigation: per-model thresholds with minimum sample size; suppress paging; document exceptions; consider region/SKU-specific thresholds only for models that demonstrably need it.

Risk: telemetry cardinality blowup / dashboard degradation.
Mitigation: adhere to label set from cardinality audit; avoid adding new dimensions during expansion; use dashboard templating and controlled panel counts.

Risk: baseline drift during fleet changes.
Mitigation: pin baselines during expansion window; annotate fleet change events on dashboards; avoid baseline refresh during known infra churn windows.
